definition: says_something — the output is a non-answer: it says nothing the asker could use. A placeholder (an ellipsis or punctuation, a program's empty value such as null or undefined, lorem ipsum); a bare acknowledgement or claim of completion where the ask needed an answer, or something written and nothing in the call shows it was written elsewhere, or an action and the call records that no tool was called; a bare refusal of an ask that it was not right to refuse; the ask handed back; one sentence repeated until it is most of the output. A short right answer, an acknowledgement that reports work the call records, and the refusal of a harmful ask are answers. Positive = a non-answer (the rule should FAIL).
source: LLM-authored on 2026-10-02 for this rule; the first twelve shapes come from an outside review's degenerate-agent probe, the rest were written to sit on either side of each shape's boundary.
labelling: LLM-authored and LLM-labelled on 2026-10-02 by reading each case against the definition before the rule was run on any of them. Where the reader and the rule's mechanism can disagree the label follows the reader and the note says so: a "null" that is the literal value asked for is an answer (says-032); declining to write a phishing email is right although no blocklisted phrase is in the ask (says-028); an ask handed back behind a short preface is a non-answer (says-013).
